name: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Linear deposition of IgA at the basement membrane zone on direct immunofluorescence
Presence of subepidermal blisters on histopathology
Tense vesicles and bullae with annular or grouped arrangement on skin
Negative or absent circulating autoantibodies to BP180 and BP230

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (linear IgA deposition, subepidermal blisters, and characteristic clinical presentation) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Direct immunofluorescence is the gold standard for diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Linear IgA deposition at basement membrane zone

common.symptomName: Erosions and crusting secondary to blister rupture

common.notes: May cause conjunctivitis or oral ulcers

laboratory: Direct immunofluorescence showing linear IgA deposits at basement membrane zone
Histopathology revealing subepidermal blister with neutrophilic infiltrate
Negative indirect immunofluorescence or ELISA for BP180 and BP230 antibodies
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; autoimmune etiology
other: Clinical response to dapsone therapy supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Linear IgG and C3 deposition instead of IgA
Granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae rather than linear at basement membrane
Pruritic papulovesicular lesions on extensor surfaces

redFlags: Rapidly progressive mucosal involvement causing airway compromise
Secondary bacterial infection with systemic signs
Ocular involvement leading to scarring and vision loss
references: Leonard JN, et al. Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis: Clinical and Immunopathologic Features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.
Zone JJ. Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis. Dermatol Clin. 2011.
Lever's Histopathology of the Skin, 11th Edition, 2014.
